newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude firmer, Dated trades at May -82 ct.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude firmer, Dated trades at May -82 ct.

text.p: A strong recovery in refining margins and the sight of April North Sea cargoes heading for the U.S. boosted benchmark Dated Brent and paper markets on Wednesday, traders said.

An April 18-20 minimum Brent cargo traded twice, first between traders at May Brent less 85 cents and then to a northwest European refiner at May Brent less 82 cents, 10 cents firmer than a deal on Tuesday.
"Everything is bid firmer this morning, paper, CFDs and the wet barrels," said a trader.
May Brent added 20 cents to $18.13 a barrel by 1022 GMT.
Intermonth spreads strengthened as the flat price rose, May/June trading 4-6 cents firmer at -16 cents and June/July trading a couple of cents higher at -9 cents.
Brent CFDs also took heart. Next week's April 14-18 dates changed hands at June Brent -60 cents, about six cents firmer than late Tuesday levels.
April 28-02 and May 5-9 also traded, at June Brent -47 cents and -42 cents respectively, dealers said.
Encouraging U.S. inventory data, which showed refined product stocks falling and refinery throughput rising last week, were helping North Sea sentiment, they said.
Shipping brokers said a U.S. refiner had fixed the VLCC Ethnic to take 260,000 tonnes transatlantic in late April.
Traders said Forties and Oseberg shipments to the U.S. were helping to clear the late April overhang of North Sea crude.
A sustained improvement in margins was also supporting North Sea sentiment but some traders said the Atlantic Basin was still well supplied and May programmes were due to be released soon.
"Physical grades have come back significantly, starting last Friday, particularly in the North Sea. Whether that works through to Nigerian crudes is another matter," said a trader.
